steps.text: Beat the cream cheese and butter in a mixer bowl until light and fluffy. Gradually add the confectioners' sugar, one cup at a time, alternating with heavy cream. Beat in the salt, coconut flavoring, and vanilla extract. Continue beating until mixture is smooth and spreadable. Add additional confectioners' sugar if necessary to thicken the frosting, or more cream to thin. Stir in the coconut. If desired, spoon toasted coconut evenly over frosted cake.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut-Cream Cheese Frosting
raw_recipe.description: Sweetened, shredded coconut adds flavor and texture to a luscious butter and cream cheese frosting that's easy to make and ever so good. Use toasted coconut as a garnish to create an extra elegant cake.
raw_recipe.name: Coconut-Cream Cheese Frosting

review.reviewBody: AMAZING RECIPE! Since I didn't have any coconut flavoring, I used some extra shredded coconut. Absolutely delicious! I use this on many cakes - carrot, white, yellow, coconut cake, coconut pound cake - everybody loves it! If you are looking for an all around good frosting that can be used on many cakes, this is the one! It is FABULOUS! You must try it.

This recipe is GREAT! My husband wanted a cream cheese and coconut frosting for his birthday cake, which I had never made before, and this one received two big thumbs up! I read through several of the reviews because I knew I would change a few things. 1. I halved the recipe for my 18 cupcakes. 2. I used vanilla extract instead of coconut extract. 3. I also used whole milk, and slowly added it after the confectioner's sugar to get the consistency I wanted. 4. I used unsweetened coconut, and added 1 tablespoon of agave nectar. It turned out great! I'll be using this recipe again!
One thing to remember is to put this on a cold cake ..if you don't it will end up melting down the side.
Amazing flavor and consistency. Love the extra twang the sour cream adds. I paid mine with strawberry cake for baby shower cupcakes! Huge hit!

This was great, but I halved the amount of powdered sugar. I also didn't need any cream to have the correct consistency with the absence of the sugar. I like being able to taste the cream cheese, and since I added all of the optional sweetened coconut, it was plenty sweet. I used this inside of a lemon sponge cake to make a jelly roll, and it was delicious.

Great recipe. However, I use only 1 2/3 cut powdered sugar and it's very sweet. I cannot imagine using 4 cups. No need for the cream. I omit it each time.
I use this for carrot cake and add 3/4 cup shredded sweetened coconut. It's great with 1/8 tsp of cinnamon and cayenne pepper (ground) also.
Would like to try it with a bit of lemon juice or extract.
As for the runny comments, I don't see how. My guess is folks may be melting the butter or microwaving the stick which will release the oils.

I've made this before and saved it because I liked it. However, I never toasted the coconut before and the difference having the toasted coconut sprinkled on top of the frosting was phenomenal. I used 3 cups of confectioners sugar, and served on a simple white cake. Wonderful.

This frosting was really good. I used it on top of the Hawaiian Wedding Cake recipe from this site and it was a hit. I would definitely suggest adding the toasted coconut on top - it seems like a small touch but it really makes a difference in the level of coconut flavor that comes through.
Great taste. Added a little more coconut and some lemon zest, which made it perfect!

Excellent frosting for a chocolate cake! A 1/2 recipe is perfect for a 13x9 cake. I made it without the coconut extract (I had none!) but I doubled the shredded coconut mixed into the frosting. There was lots of coconut and lots of coconut flavor! So yummy!

Absolutely awesome. Very smooth and creamy without being too sweet. The only change I made I took from another reviewer of another cream cheese frosting. For those who are having trouble with the frosting being too thin, I beat the butter and powdered sugar added cream and flavor then added COLD cream cheese in small bits. My frosting came together quickly without added powdered sugar, perfect consistently. I will always use cold cream cheese from now on. Thanks for the great recipe.
I ended up not adding any heavy cream and using the tiniest amount of milk. The frosting tastes heavenly

Oh wow, this is good! I made my own birthday cake with a pineapple upside down cake, cake mix. I like sponge/angel food cake so I whipped 5 egg whites and added it to the cake batter at the end before I made this coconut-cream cheese frosting. Like some others, I didn't add as much confectioner's sugar and instead of coconut cream, I added Spiced Rum. I had made some whipped cream for the filling and added a couple of tablespoons of it to the frosting at the end. The consistency was very fluffy and one of the easiest frosts I've ever done! It kept its consistency on the cooled cake layers. Dusted the top with toasted coconut and it was beautiful! I love my birthday cake!

This turned out beautifully, and as other reviewers mentioned, it’s flexibility allows you to work your own touch to it. I don’t believe I used a full four cups of powdered sugar, I just added til it looked thick and smooth.
This is good as is, but we added a few tablespoons of cocoa powder to it and it was next level!

Loved it, and it hasn't even gone on my cake yet. I didn't have any cream, so I used orange juice, instead, and I used one teaspoon each of vanilla, orange, and coconut flavoring. This will go on a pound cake having all the same flavors-if there is any left after the cake comes out of the oven.
perfect match for the gluten free cake
Delicious! Perfect consistency & great taste, didn’t have to tweak it at all. I topped it with toasted coconut & pecans - yummy!
